title: Microsoft Purview: auto-expanding archive limit rising from 1.5 TB to 3 TB for eligible mailboxes (GCC, GCC High, DoD)
summary: Hold: the shared-mailbox question presents eligibility as unpublished, although Microsoft's mailbox-wide licence rule covers shared mailboxes. The government rollout dates, automatic increase for eligible enabled archives, licensing list and PowerShell controls are supported.

claims.where: title; summary; What's changing; Why it matters; Scope; Governance guidance; rationales
claims.claim: Eligible Exchange Online archive mailboxes with auto-expanding archiving enabled can grow from the previous 1.5 TB ceiling to a maximum of 3 TB per mailbox.
claims.quote: Eligible archive mailboxes with auto-expanding archiving enabled can automatically expand beyond the current 1.5 TB limit, up to a maximum of 3 TB per mailbox.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; What's changing; Why it matters; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The increased ceiling arrives automatically for eligible mailboxes that already have auto-expanding archiving enabled, supporting defaultState on.
claims.quote: No additional configuration is required for eligible mailboxes that already have auto-expanding archiving enabled.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model and licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The increased capacity is included with an eligible assigned licence, such as Office 365 E5 or Microsoft 365 E5.
claims.quote:
The increase applies to mailboxes assigned the following eligible licenses:
- Office 365 E5, A5, or G5
- Microsoft 365 E5, A5, or G5

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; Cost and licensing; Governance guidance; rationales
claims.claim: Mailboxes without an eligible licence retain the existing 1.5 TB ceiling.
claims.quote: For all other licenses, the existing 1.5 TB limit remains unchanged.

claims.claim: MC1521615 was published on 22 October 2026.
claims.quote: Published 2026-10-22; last updated 2026-10-22

claims.claim: MC1521615 gives General Availability rollout beginning in mid-November 2026 for GCC, GCC High and DoD.
claims.quote: General Availability (GCC, GCC High, DoD): Rollout will begin in mid-November 2026

claims.claim: MC1521615 expects government rollout to complete by early December 2026.
claims.quote: is expected to complete by early December 2026.

claims.claim: The supplied notice sets no act-by date.
claims.quote: Act by: none

claims.claim: The Learn archive pages give a rollout beginning in mid-October 2026.
claims.quote: Rollout begins in mid-October 2026

claims.claim: The Learn archive pages expect rollout to complete by late October 2026.
claims.quote: Rollout begins in mid-October 2026 and is expected to complete by late October.

claims.claim: The rollout banners on the two cited Learn pages name no clouds.
claims.quote: Searched: "auto-expanding archiving" "mid-October 2026" "GCC"; opened learn.microsoft.com/purview/enable-autoexpanding-archiving and /purview/autoexpanding-archiving in full. Neither banner names clouds.

claims.claim: The overview's body text still describes a 1.5 TB maximum, despite its new 3 TB banner.
claims.quote: Microsoft Purview automatically (and incrementally) increases the size of the archive until the archive mailbox reaches 1.5 TB.

claims.claim: Eligible enabled archives gain capacity without a support request once the change reaches the tenant.
claims.quote: without requiring manual archive expansion processes or support requests. Eligible mailboxes with auto-expanding archiving enabled will continue to grow automatically as needed.

claims.where: Why it matters; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft recommends reviewing licence assignments for users with large archive mailboxes.
claims.quote: Review license assignments for users with large archive mailboxes to confirm eligibility.

claims.where: Why it matters; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft recommends updating internal documentation, retention guidance and help desk materials.
claims.quote: Update internal documentation, retention guidance, and help desk materials to reflect the new 3 TB limit.

claims.where: Why it matters; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft recommends reviewing licensing and retention strategies for users whose archives are not eligible.
claims.quote: Review licensing and retention strategies for users whose archive mailboxes are not eligible for the expanded capacity.

claims.claim: Learn continues to limit supported archive growth to no more than 1 GB per day.
claims.quote: Auto-expanding archiving is supported only for mailboxes used for individual users (or shared mailboxes) with a growth rate that doesn't exceed 1 GB per day.

claims.claim: eDiscovery tools such as Content Search search the additional storage areas of auto-expanded archives.
claims.quote: When you use an eDiscovery tool, such as Content Search, the additional storage areas in an auto-expanded archive are also searched.

claims.claim: Mailbox holds also cover content in an auto-expanded archive.
claims.quote: When you put a mailbox on hold by using methods such as Microsoft 365 retention, eDiscovery case holds, and Litigation Hold in Exchange Online, content located in an auto-expanded archive is also placed on hold.

claims.claim: The change's documentation describes no new permission or identity.
claims.quote: Searched: "auto-expanding archiving" "3 TB" permissions identity. Read MC1521615 and both cited Learn pages; the increase names licence eligibility and existing enablement, not a new identity or permission.

claims.claim: Organisation-wide enablement requires a global administrator or Organization Management role group member.
claims.quote: you must be a global administrator in your organization or a member of the Organization Management role group in your Exchange Online organization.

claims.claim: A member of a role group including Mail Recipients can alternatively enable auto-expanding archiving for specific users.
claims.quote: Alternately, to enable auto-expanding archiving for specific users, you must be a member of a role group that includes the Mail Recipients role.

claims.claim: Additional archive storage is added automatically when auto-expanding archiving is on.
claims.quote: The additional storage creation happens automatically, which means administrators don't have to request additional archive storage or manage auto-expanding archiving.

claims.where: controls[0].note; controls[1].note; Risk assessment; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Auto-expanding archiving cannot be turned off after organisation-wide or per-user enablement.
claims.quote: After you turn on auto-expanding archiving for your organization or for a specific user, it can't be turned off.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance controls
claims.claim: Administrators cannot adjust the auto-expanding archive storage quota.
claims.quote: Administrators can't adjust the storage quota for auto-expanding archiving.

claims.claim: For E5 licences, Learn says to verify that Records Management is selected and remains enabled in the user's licence settings.
claims.quote: For E5 licenses, verify that Records Management is selected and remains enabled in the user's license settings.

claims.claim: Once an auto-expanded storage area has been provisioned, users cannot delete folders from the archive.
claims.quote: after an auto-expanded storage area has been provisioned, they can't delete any folders in the archive.

claims.claim: Auto-expanding archiving prevents recovery of an inactive mailbox.
claims.quote: Auto-expanding archiving prevents you from recovering or restoring an inactive mailbox.

claims.claim: Auto-expanding archiving prevents restoration of an inactive mailbox.
claims.quote: Auto-expanding archiving prevents you from recovering or restoring an inactive mailbox.

claims.claim: Office 365 E5, A5 and G5 are eligible licences.
claims.quote: Office 365 E5, A5, or G5

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 E5, A5 and G5 are eligible licences.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 E5, A5, or G5

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 Purview Suite is eligible.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 Purview Suite

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 Purview Suite FLW, EDU and GOV are eligible.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 Purview Suite FLW, EDU, or GOV

claims.claim: Microsoft Defender + Purview Suite FLW is eligible.
claims.quote: Microsoft Defender + Purview Suite FLW

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 F5 Compliance is eligible.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 F5 Compliance

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 F5 Security + Compliance is eligible.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 F5 Security + Compliance

claims.claim: The combination of the eDiscovery & Audit, Insider Risk Management and Information Protection & Governance mini suites is eligible.
claims.quote: The combination of the eDiscovery & Audit, Insider Risk Management, and Information Protection & Governance mini suites

claims.claim: Qualifying offerings including Purview E5 capabilities, such as E7, also support the increased limit.
claims.quote: Qualifying offerings that include Microsoft Purview E5 capabilities, such as E7, also support the increase.

claims.claim: The two cited Learn archive pages state no price for moving a user to an eligible licence.
claims.quote: Searched: "auto-expanding archiving" "price" "per-GB". Opened learn.microsoft.com/purview/enable-autoexpanding-archiving and /purview/autoexpanding-archiving in full; they list eligible licences and no upgrade price.

claims.claim: Auto-expanding archiving supports shared mailboxes.
claims.quote: Auto-expanding archiving also supports shared mailboxes.

claims.claim: The user's archive mailbox must already be enabled before enabling auto-expanding archiving.
claims.quote: A user's mailbox must already be enabled for archive before you can enable auto-expanding archiving.

claims.claim: Cloud-based archives for users with on-premises primary mailboxes are supported in Exchange hybrid deployments.
claims.quote: Auto-expanding archiving is supported for cloud-based archive mailboxes in an Exchange hybrid deployment for users who have an on-premises primary mailbox.

claims.claim: Auto-expanding archiving is not supported for on-premises mailboxes.
claims.quote: Auto-expanding archiving isn't supported for on-premises mailboxes in any version of Exchange Server.

claims.claim: There is no documented admin-centre UI for organisation-wide auto-expanding archiving enablement.
claims.quote: Searched: "auto-expanding archiving" "admin center" "specific users". Read Enable auto-expanding archiving: "You can't use the Exchange admin center or the Microsoft Purview portal to enable auto-expanding archiving. You must use Exchange Online PowerShell."

claims.claim: Set-OrganizationConfig -AutoExpandingArchive in Exchange Online PowerShell enables auto-expanding archiving for the whole organisation.
claims.quote:
To enable auto-expanding archiving for your entire organization, run the following command:
Set-OrganizationConfig -AutoExpandingArchive

claims.claim: There is no documented admin-centre UI for per-user auto-expanding archiving enablement.
claims.quote: Searched: "auto-expanding archiving" "admin center" "specific users". Read Enable auto-expanding archiving: it prohibits Exchange admin center and Purview portal enablement and gives only Exchange Online PowerShell for specific users.

claims.claim: Enable-Mailbox <user mailbox> -AutoExpandingArchive in Exchange Online PowerShell enables auto-expanding archiving for a specific cloud user.
claims.quote:
To enable auto-expanding archiving for a specific user, run the following command.
Enable-Mailbox <user mailbox> -AutoExpandingArchive

claims.claim: The per-user command requires cloud primary and archive mailboxes; an on-premises primary with a cloud archive requires the organisation-wide command.
claims.quote: If a user's primary and archive mailboxes are both cloud-based, then you can use the Enable-Mailbox -AutoExpandingArchive command to enable auto-expanding archiving for that specific user.

claims.claim: Get-OrganizationConfig | FL AutoExpandingArchiveEnabled checks organisation-wide enablement.
claims.quote:
To verify that auto-expanding archiving is enabled for your organization, run the following command in Exchange Online PowerShell.
Get-OrganizationConfig | FL AutoExpandingArchiveEnabled

claims.claim: Get-Mailbox <user mailbox> | FL AutoExpandingArchiveEnabled checks per-user enablement.
claims.quote:
To verify that auto-expanding archiving is enabled for a specific user, run the following command in Exchange Online PowerShell.
Get-Mailbox <user mailbox> | FL AutoExpandingArchiveEnabled

claims.claim: Organisation-wide enablement does not set AutoExpandingArchiveEnabled to True on individual user mailbox objects.
claims.quote: Running the Set-OrganizationConfig cmdlet to enable auto-expanding archiving for your organization doesn't change the AutoExpandingArchiveEnabled property on user mailboxes to True.

claims.claim: Neither enablement control selects the 1.5 TB or 3 TB ceiling.
claims.quote: Administrators can't adjust the storage quota for auto-expanding archiving.

claims.claim: Per-user enablement for a mailbox on hold or assigned a retention policy adds 10 GB to the primary archive quota.
claims.quote: When you enable auto-expanding archiving for a specific user and the user's mailbox in on hold or assigned to a retention policy ... The storage quota for the user's primary archive mailbox is increased by 10 GB (from 100 GB to 110 GB).

claims.claim: Whether shared mailboxes qualify for 3 TB and which assigned licence decides their eligibility remain undocumented.
claims.quote: The increase applies to mailboxes assigned the following eligible licenses: ... Auto-expanding archiving also supports shared mailboxes.
claims.fix: Remove the first Open questions bullet. The cited page includes shared mailboxes in auto-expanding archiving and applies the increased ceiling to mailboxes assigned the listed eligible licences; it does not exclude shared mailboxes from that rule.

claims.claim: The change's pages do not state what happens to an archive already above 1.5 TB when its eligible licence is removed.
claims.quote: Searched: "auto-expanding" "3 TB" license removed downgrade. Read both cited archive pages in full; they state the ceiling for other licences but not treatment of an already oversized archive after licence removal.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout, first bullet
claims.claim: The checklist tells administrators to check assigned licences, but the controls table contains no licence-assignment control.
claims.quote: check which licence each holds against the eligible list in Cost and licensing; controls: Auto-expanding archiving for the whole organisation; Auto-expanding archiving for specific users
claims.fix: Remove the first Before rollout checklist bullet, which tells readers to check licence assignments without a corresponding control row. Keep the existing licensing explanation and Microsoft's recommendation in Why it matters.

controlChecks.governs: Auto-expanding archiving for the whole organisation
